status: PROPOSED module-level source decisions for H1 arm B (2026-10-21 UTC), from a $0 desk audit of primary sources and a $0 local validation of 5 instances per module per difficulty (pinned installs in an isolated scratch environment). Decisions are proposals for the maintainer; adopting any third-party generator is also a dependency decision. Nothing here is downloaded into the repository or generated at scale.
verification_policy: a library score is NEVER the correctness verdict: many scorers give partial credit (near-miss wrong answers scored 0.84-0.999), five reasoning-gym scorers evaluate the answer text as Python (string_insertion, spiral_matrix, binary_matrix, n_queens via eval; countdown via sympy parse_expr), and must never see teacher output

arm B uses a PROJECT-SIDE exact check per module: canonical exact match against the generator's gold, or, where several answers are valid, a project validity checker (simulation, constraint check); score_answer may only be consulted on the generator's own gold during the audit

instances are generated ONCE, with PYTHONHASHSEED and every seed pinned, in a fresh process per module, and STORED as task files; nothing is regenerated later (several modules depend on the hash seed, the global RNG, process history or the wall clock)

reference proofs and solution traces (PrOntoQA chain_of_thought, reasoning-core metadata.cot, string_manipulation states) are used ONLY to verify the teacher's process; they never enter a prompt and never become a target

It still calls ndarray.itemset, which numpy 2 removed, so it runs in its own isolated venv: numpy 1.26.4, sympy 1.14.0, absl-py 2.5.1, six 1.17.0, mpmath 1.3.0 (export run 2026-10-22). mathematics_dataset.dependency_note: no answer checker ships; answers are canonical strings. The composed modules' statement ORDER varies across processes even with every seed and PYTHONHASHSEED pinned (object-identity ordering in its composition code; measured 2026-10-22: 14 of 56 sample prompts reordered between two runs, no answer changed), so instances are generated once and stored and the export file's sha256 is their identity

mechanism_review.method: declared per candidate module from its documentation and the validation samples, against every eval-set-1 held-out family and evaluation-only generator; the tabulated project families are checked by execution instead (mechanism_check.py, isolation rule R9)

exposure.shares_primitive: a step or primitive an evaluation family also uses, in another format or stated rather than induced: REPORTED, and the affected evaluation tier is read with it
exposure.equivalent: the module teaches an evaluation family's rule itself: excluded

presentation.explicit_rule: the rule is stated in the prompt; a held-out INDUCTIVE family with the same rule would be the main exposure risk -- none found
presentation.induction: the rule is to be discovered

mechanism_review.found: no candidate module computes an evaluation family's rule; 7 share a primitive (listed per module); the explicit-rule modules state rotations, traversals and rewrites, none of which is a held-out inductive rule
mechanism_review.limits: a declared review, not an execution check: it can miss a mechanism a module's generator produces only at some configurations

answer_types.number_set: the same multiset of numbers within 1e-6
answer_types.matrix: the same token grid (rows of tokens)
answer_types.needs_checker: no project check exists: every candidate would be UNVERIFIABLE, so a module of this type is not a candidate (deferred) and enters no paid generation list
answer_types.checker: a project checker in scripts/stages/stage-2/reasoning_data/checkers.py (CHECKERS, keyed source/module): a validity check or simulation, or value equality through a safe parser; never a library scorer, never evaluation of answer text

_drop_if_gold_in_prompt: only where the gold appearing verbatim in the prompt means a degenerate item (the answer IS the input: an unchanged string, an identity rotation); for choice and selection modules the gold is one of the listed options by construction
_levels: a row's levels are what the exporter generates (default 0 and 2, the library difficulty levels of reasoning_gym / reasoning_core); prontoqa: hop counts; mathematics_dataset: train entropy levels 1 (medium) and 2 (hard)
